topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Traditional Cancer Modalities and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine conventional cancer interventions—chiefly surgery, radiation, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with the severe toxicities and drug resistance mechanisms they entail.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies designed to exploit the inherent biological vulnerabilities and specific molecular defects of cancer cells.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on designing small-molecule inhibitors to target hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and addressing the subsequent emergence of drug resistance and bypass signaling.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe using engineered antibodies to target cancer cell surface proteins directly or to selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and Cellular Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate tumor immune surveillance and examine immunotherapeutic strategies that harness, reactivate, or genetically engineer T cells to eliminate cancer.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic challenges, historical survival trends, emerging approaches, and clinical dilemmas shaping the future of cancer therapy.
